            "Downloading Suspense 0.1.N…" when a newer release is found,

            machine, it is disabled, its tooltip saying why, as the Updates
            section does. Otherwise its tooltip says it checks for a newer
            version of Suspense.

            It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon
            leaves it out.

use /lib
use /ui
from /scope/settings-window import SettingsWindowScope
from /scope/user-preferences import UserPreferencesScope
from /scope/walkthrough import WalkthroughScope
from /scope/welcome import WelcomeScope
from /ui/components/theme-editor import ThemeEditorScope
from /ui/theme import ThemeScope

export ui-component RibbonApplicationTabScope:
    concept: {RibbonApplicationTabConcept}

concept RibbonApplicationTabConcept:
    pitch:
        The ribbon's Application tab: the commands for the application itself,
        rather than the project.

    shape: {RibbonApplicationTabShape}

shape RibbonApplicationTabShape:
    description:
        The Application tab of the ribbon, last of the tabs.

    groups:
        appearance:
            An "Appearance" group holds the Brightness command, its one
            control; there is no Dark mode switch, since the slider reaches
            both modes.

        colours:
            A "Colours" group, between Appearance and Preferences, holds the
            Theme command.

        preferences:
            A "Preferences" group holds the Settings command.

        help:
            A "Help" group, the last, after Preferences, holds the Welcome
            command, then the Walkthrough command.

    commands:
        brightness:
            A "Brightness" slider, which runs the whole interface from its
            darkest to its lightest: a moon icon, then a horizontal slider
            120 pixels wide, then a sun icon, with nothing showing the setting
            as a number. As a ribbon setting, it has no background of its
            own, and sits straight on the commands' area, as tall as a slim
            button. Its tooltip says it makes the whole interface darker or
            lighter, from its darkest to its lightest, keeping its contrast,
            and that double-clicking it resets it.

            Its one track runs through every appearance the @{ThemeScope}
            allows, darkest first: dark mode from its darkest brightness to
            its lightest, then light mode from its darkest to its lightest,
            one position for each step, with no switch between them. So all
            the way left is dark mode at its darkest, and all the way right
            light mode at its lightest; dragging past dark mode's lightest
            step changes the window to light mode, and back.

            Dragging it changes the mode and the brightness straight away as
            it moves, and once it is let go saves the mode showing and each
            mode's brightness among the @{UserPreferencesScope}. A mode that
            can't be saved shows a notification titled
            "Could not save brightness", with why; a brightness that can't be
            saved fails quietly. Its thumb follows the appearance showing,
            however that was changed, such as from the palette, but not while
            it is being dragged.

            Double-clicking anywhere on it, its icons or its track, puts the
            mode showing back to its brightness at 0, keeping the mode, and
            saves it; the second click doesn't also move the thumb.

            It is primary, so the collapsed ribbon keeps it: its icons and
            track as they are, only as wide as they are, as tall as a small
            button.

        theme:
            A "Theme" button with a palette icon. Clicking it opens the
            @{ThemeEditorScope}. Its tooltip says it chooses the base colour,
            and the colours of Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask.

            It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon
            leaves it out.

        settings:
            A "Settings" button with a gear icon. Clicking it opens the
            @{SettingsWindowScope}, where the system prompt each chat tab sends
            is edited. Its tooltip says so, and gives its keyboard shortcut,
            Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS).

            It is primary, and a full button.

        welcome:
            A "Welcome" button with a checklist icon. Clicking it opens the
            @{WelcomeScope}, running its checks anew. Its tooltip says it
            checks that Suspense is ready to run.

            It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon
            leaves it out.

        walkthrough:
            A "Walkthrough" button with a signpost icon. Clicking it starts
            the @{WalkthroughScope} from its first step. Its tooltip says it
            walks through creating a project and the prompt modes.

            It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon
            leaves it out.

use /lib
use /ui
from /scope/self-update import SelfUpdateScope
from /scope/settings-window import SettingsWindowScope
from /scope/user-preferences import UserPreferencesScope
from /scope/walkthrough import WalkthroughScope
from /scope/welcome import WelcomeScope
from /ui/components/theme-editor import ThemeEditorScope
from /ui/theme import ThemeScope

export ui-component RibbonApplicationTabScope:
    concept: {RibbonApplicationTabConcept}

concept RibbonApplicationTabConcept:
    pitch:
        The ribbon's Application tab: the commands for the application itself,
        rather than the project.

    shape: {RibbonApplicationTabShape}

shape RibbonApplicationTabShape:
    description:
        The Application tab of the ribbon, last of the tabs.

    groups:
        appearance:
            An "Appearance" group holds the Brightness command, its one
            control; there is no Dark mode switch, since the slider reaches
            both modes.

        colours:
            A "Colours" group, between Appearance and Preferences, holds the
            Theme command.

        preferences:
            A "Preferences" group holds the Settings command.

        help:
            A "Help" group, the last, after Preferences, holds the Welcome
            command, then the Walkthrough command, then the Check for Updates
            command.

    commands:
        brightness:
            A "Brightness" slider, which runs the whole interface from its
            darkest to its lightest: a moon icon, then a horizontal slider
            120 pixels wide, then a sun icon, with nothing showing the setting
            as a number. As a ribbon setting, it has no background of its
            own, and sits straight on the commands' area, as tall as a slim
            button. Its tooltip says it makes the whole interface darker or
            lighter, from its darkest to its lightest, keeping its contrast,
            and that double-clicking it resets it.

            Its one track runs through every appearance the @{ThemeScope}
            allows, darkest first: dark mode from its darkest brightness to
            its lightest, then light mode from its darkest to its lightest,
            one position for each step, with no switch between them. So all
            the way left is dark mode at its darkest, and all the way right
            light mode at its lightest; dragging past dark mode's lightest
            step changes the window to light mode, and back.

            Dragging it changes the mode and the brightness straight away as
            it moves, and once it is let go saves the mode showing and each
            mode's brightness among the @{UserPreferencesScope}. A mode that
            can't be saved shows a notification titled
            "Could not save brightness", with why; a brightness that can't be
            saved fails quietly. Its thumb follows the appearance showing,
            however that was changed, such as from the palette, but not while
            it is being dragged.

            Double-clicking anywhere on it, its icons or its track, puts the
            mode showing back to its brightness at 0, keeping the mode, and
            saves it; the second click doesn't also move the thumb.

            It is primary, so the collapsed ribbon keeps it: its icons and
            track as they are, only as wide as they are, as tall as a small
            button.

        theme:
            A "Theme" button with a palette icon. Clicking it opens the
            @{ThemeEditorScope}. Its tooltip says it chooses the base colour,
            and the colours of Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask.

            It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon
            leaves it out.

        settings:
            A "Settings" button with a gear icon. Clicking it opens the
            @{SettingsWindowScope}, where the system prompt each chat tab sends
            is edited. Its tooltip says so, and gives its keyboard shortcut,
            Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS).

            It is primary, and a full button.

        welcome:
            A "Welcome" button with a checklist icon. Clicking it opens the
            @{WelcomeScope}, running its checks anew. Its tooltip says it
            checks that Suspense is ready to run.

            It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon
            leaves it out.

        walkthrough:
            A "Walkthrough" button with a signpost icon. Clicking it starts
            the @{WalkthroughScope} from its first step. Its tooltip says it
            walks through creating a project and the prompt modes.

            It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon
            leaves it out.

        checkForUpdates:
            A "Check for Updates" button with a refresh icon. Clicking it
            checks for an update straight away, as the Updates section's
            Check for updates does, as the @{SelfUpdateScope} says, whether
            automatic checks are on or not, and says how it went in a
            notification: "Suspense is up to date", with the version running;
            "Downloading Suspense 0.1.N…" when a newer release is found,
            followed by the "Suspense 0.1.N is ready" notification, with its
            Restart and Later buttons, once it is staged; or, titled
            "Could not check for updates", why the check or download failed.

            While a check or download is under way, it shows a spinner in
            place of its icon and is disabled, its tooltip saying what is
            under way. While an update is already staged, clicking it shows
            the "Suspense 0.1.N is ready" notification again, without checking.
            In a build that can't update itself, as one made on a developer's
            machine, it is disabled, its tooltip saying why, as the Updates
            section does. Otherwise its tooltip says it checks for a newer
            version of Suspense.

            It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon
            leaves it out.

content.text:
I've added a **Check for Updates** button to the Application tab's Help group, after Welcome and Walkthrough. `piton check` reports no problems, the file is formatted, and `piton build` succeeds. I confirmed the button and the group change in the refreshed reference.

**How it works:**
- **Click:** checks for an update straight away, exactly as the Settings → Updates button does, whether or not automatic checks are on. The result appears as a notification:
  - "Suspense is up to date", with the running version.
  - "Downloading Suspense 0.1.N…", followed by the existing "Suspense 0.1.N is ready" notification with **Restart** and **Later** once the update is staged.
  - "Could not check for updates", with the reason.
- **While checking or downloading:** a spinner replaces the icon, the button is disabled, and the tooltip says what's happening.
- **Update already downloaded:** clicking shows the "ready" notification again instead of checking.
- **Builds that can't update themselves, such as a local dev build:** the button is disabled, with a tooltip explaining why.

It's a full, non-primary button with a refresh icon, so the collapsed ribbon leaves it out.

## What changed in the spec, and the anchors the code should follow

- **`RibbonApplicationTabShape.groups.help`:** the Help group now holds Welcome, Walkthrough, then Check for Updates.
- **`RibbonApplicationTabShape.commands.checkForUpdates` (new):**
  - Reuse the existing manual check from `SelfUpdateShape.checking`, `.downloading` and `.restarting`, the same code path as the Updates section's button.
  - Show the result in the notifications listed above.
  - Show a spinner and disable the button while a check or download runs.
  - With an update already staged, re-show the ready notification without checking.
  - In builds without a baked-in repository, disable the button and give the reason in its tooltip.
